title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
claim: Encapsulating one nanosized heterometallic cluster in a silica nanoshell gives monodisperse core–shell particles that stabilize the molecule, reduce magnetic interactions between clusters, and slightly increase −ΔSM relative to the unprotected parent.
explanation: A microemulsion route produced Gd52Ni56@SiO2 particles, each described as one cluster inside one silica shell. The composite −ΔSM is a 10% enhancement over the parent value of 40.5 J kg−1 K−1; the composite figure is split in the Markdown as “4 . 6”, consistent with 44.6. Theory is cited for reduced intercluster coupling. For Gd12Fe14@SiO2, silica is also said to decrease intermolecular coupling while increasing zero-field splitting of outer Fe(III) ions.
scope: Processable silica-passivated nanoparticles of individual high-nuclearity 3d–4f molecular clusters, illustrated for Ni–Gd and Fe–Gd clusters.
conditions: Microemulsion encapsulation; one cluster core per silica nanoshell; MCE compared with the unprotected crystalline or bulk cluster.
caveats: Described as a preliminary, system-specific attempt. The enhancement is small, and increased Fe(III) zero-field splitting is an additional effect that is not claimed to be generally beneficial for MCE.
evidence_locations: Conspectus; end of Section 3.2; Figure 10; refs 28, 33
